column1: # The SVG 2 presentation attributes: which attribute sets which property, on which elements, and how the attribute is spelled.
# Source: SVG 2, 6.6 "Presentation attributes" (https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG2/styling.html, Candidate Recommendation Draft, served 2026-10-26),
# the table "Properties with a presentation attribute":
#   "cx, cy" on circle and ellipse; "height, width, x, y" on foreignObject, image, rect, svg, symbol and use; "r" on circle; "rx, ry" on
#   ellipse and rect; "d" on path; "fill"; "transform" (also patternTransform and gradientTransform); and, on any element in the SVG
#   namespace: "alignment-baseline, baseline-shift, clip-path, clip-rule, color, color-interpolation, color-interpolation-filters, cursor,
#   direction, display, dominant-baseline, fill-opacity, fill-rule, filter, flood-color, flood-opacity, font-family, font-size,
#   font-size-adjust, font-stretch, font-style, font-variant, font-weight, glyph-orientation-vertical, image-rendering, letter-spacing,
#   lighting-color, marker-end, marker-mid, marker-start, mask, mask-type, opacity, overflow, paint-order, pointer-events, shape-rendering,
#   stop-color, stop-opacity, stroke, stroke-dasharray, stroke-dashoffset, stroke-linecap, stroke-linejoin, stroke-miterlimit,
#   stroke-opacity, stroke-width, text-anchor, text-decoration, text-overflow, text-rendering, transform-origin, unicode-bidi,
#   attribute   the attribute's name, case-sensitive (SVG attribute names are: patternTransform).
#   property    the property it sets (a longhand or an alias of the registry).
#   namespace   svg: only an element in the SVG namespace; *: an element in any namespace.
#   elements    *: every element; else the local names (case-sensitive), separated by commas; a list that starts with ! is every element but those.
#               (SVG 2, served 2026-10-26: fill is "any SVG-namespace element except animation elements, which have their own fill attribute";
#               transform is any SVG-namespace element except pattern, linearGradient and radialGradient.)
#   syntax      css: the attribute's value is the property's value; transform: the SVG transform list syntax (or the property's, the
#               attribute-only spelling is an option); path: path data, which the property `d` holds as path("...").
# Every property of this list must also be in svg_presentation.txt (the properties that must be computable), and the other way round; the
# generator (gen-presentation-table.py) holds the two together and writes src/css/tables/css_tables_presentation.c from this file.
# A caller who needs another list (HTML's presentational hints, an SVG profile) passes a table of its own in the options.
